paths.description: Public discovery homepage and primary browse entry point; tested as the highest-traffic listing surface.
British models category, representing category and search/listing templates.
About page, representing text/legal/informational content and footer navigation.
Account creation entry, representing registration and CAPTCHA-gated form UI. Account creation itself was not performed.
Login and invalid-submit state, representing authentication and form assistance.

findings.summary: The fixed dark palette is not integrated with the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark the page remains usable, but the computed root color-scheme is normal and the loaded stylesheets are dark-only; native controls cannot consistently inherit an explicit scheme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme in early metadata and on :root, then expose preference-aware light/dark tokens using light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: Non-essential animation remains active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reported two 250 ms SidebarFadeIn animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule to remove non-essential fades and transitions while preserving state feedback.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences and baseline contrast are not fully supported.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found seven color-contrast failures; the high-contrast capture shows the same authored palette rather than preference-aware system colors.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the reported foreground/background pairs and use forced-colors or prefers-contrast adjustments without suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use declarative transition primitives.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules; the public listing, category and account surfaces swap without a transition contract.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route/state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state or direct attention after route changes.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no scroll-state, scroll-timeline, or view-transition implementation; the long feed uses static chrome with no progress or post-navigation cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll-state-aware header treatment or progress where it improves orientation, and preserve a clear active route/focus cue.

findings.summary: Consent and age-verification chrome consume a large share of the first viewport.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show an age banner plus a persistent cookie panel; on mobile the cookie panel overlays the content grid and gives Accept All the dominant action.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise the consent surface, provide equally prominent choices, reserve space where a legal age notice is required, and use a semantic dismissible dialog only when modality is necessary.

findings.summary: Reusable feed and navigation components rely on viewport CSS rather than container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero container-query rules while the same card/navigation patterns are reused across desktop and mobile layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment for reusable card/nav regions and adapt them with @container where their available space, not the viewport, determines layout.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and small controls make non-pointer use difficult.
findings.evidence: The active focus probe found outline-style none and no box shadow for the first 20 focusable elements; 18 visible interactive targets were under 24 px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and enlarge compact controls or their hit areas to at least the WCAG minimum, ideally 44 CSS px for primary touch targets.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return an empty, nonstandard failure response with no recovery UI.
findings.evidence: A request to a representative nonexistent path returned HTTP 406 with an empty body, offering no explanation, home link, search, or retry path.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a useful 404 page with normal navigation, search/browse recovery, and an accurate HTTP status.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance and visual stability miss the Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.7 s, CLS 0.125, and TBT 760 ms; the independent mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.1276.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reserve media/banner geometry, and reduce startup JavaScript and long tasks; verify with repeat mobile traces.

findings.summary: The initial page ships a heavy dependency graph dominated by JavaScript and third-party assets.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 158 requests and 2,459,295 transferred bytes, including 1,353,085 bytes of script and 2,296,321 third-party bytes; the largest bootstrap script alone transferred 724,265 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the bootstrap by route, defer optional player/analytics code until intent, reduce font variants, and keep only critical CSS in the initial chain.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped CSS and JavaScript are unused on the audited route.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,150 KiB of unused JavaScript and 124 KiB of unused CSS, consistent with the large shared bootstrap observed in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route/component-level code splitting, remove legacy/shared modules from the discovery entry path, and measure coverage after each split.

findings.summary: Many links and buttons have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe counted 27 unnamed anchors and three unnamed buttons; Lighthouse independently failed link-name on ten sampled nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon-only controls an accessible name, ensure card anchors derive a meaningful name, and keep visible and accessible labels aligned.

findings.summary: Heading order and focus visibility do not provide a dependable keyboard structure.
findings.evidence: The homepage heading sequence starts H2, then H1, then H2, and focused controls computed to outline none with no compensating box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Place the page H1 before section H2 headings, simplify repeated navigation landmarks, and implement a consistent :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: Secondary and footer copy is cramped and low contrast.
findings.evidence: The About screenshot shows dense 12–14 px gray copy and low-emphasis links on a dark surface; Lighthouse also found seven contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase secondary text contrast and line-height, avoid 12 px body copy, and constrain paragraphs to a comfortable line length.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions and many are substantially oversized.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 36 images missing width/height, 17 oversized, 22 without srcset, and 15 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or aspect-ratio), responsive srcset/sizes, and lazy-load below-fold cards while keeping the LCP candidate eager.

findings.summary: The page triggers deprecated API, BFCache, and inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecation warnings, one BFCache failure reason, and Chrome inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API calls, resolve the recorded inspector issues, and eliminate avoidable unload or other BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Important content is nearly invisible to non-JavaScript crawlers and some anchors are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: The discoverability run received HTTP 403 for raw HTML, found only 5% rendered-word coverage, no raw title/H1/description, and classified the page as a JS shell; Lighthouse also failed one crawlable-anchor audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful listing text and metadata in the initial HTML to permitted crawlers, return a crawler-accessible success response, and replace non-href navigation with real links.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete despite HTTPS.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no response CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. The cookie audit found 21 of 26 cookies without Secure; the meta CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Send a nonce/hash-based CSP as a response header, add nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite setting.

findings.summary: The anonymous landing page has an outsized third-party and fingerprinting footprint.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributed 143 requests and 2,296,321 bytes to third-party origins, while the DOM loaded FingerprintJS2 and the tracker probe observed nine third-party origins before consent was accepted.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential analytics/fingerprinting behind consent, remove redundant third parties, and batch/minimise anonymous telemetry.

findings.summary: Authentication exposes password-only fields with no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login probe found username/email and password fields, no navigator.credentials/PublicKeyCredential usage in the page, and no explicit autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer WebAuthn/passkeys alongside a password fallback and add correct username/current-password autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Core public content depends on JavaScript and bot-sensitive rendering.
findings.evidence: The no-JavaScript/raw fetch returned 403 and only 5% of rendered words, with no title, H1, or description in raw content; the crawler view shows skeletons rather than useful listings.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core headings, navigation, listing summaries and recovery states, then hydrate enhancements progressively without withholding public content.

findings.summary: The observed HTTP failure state is blank rather than recoverable.
findings.evidence: The representative unknown route returned 406 with an empty response instead of a resilient not-found page.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an intentional 404 surface with retained navigation, helpful explanation, and retry/search options.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually asymmetric.
findings.evidence: The cookie panel makes Accept All a bright primary action while Manage is muted and there is no equally direct Reject All action in the first layer.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept and Reject with equal prominence, keep granular management available, and avoid loading nonessential tracking before a choice.

findings.summary: Login fields omit autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The login probe found empty autocomplete values for username/email and password, and the signup/login controls rely on placeholders instead of persistent visible labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels and autocomplete=username/current-password (and new-password where applicable); preserve password-manager and paste support.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and risks layout work.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 17 oversized images, 22 without responsive sources, 15 legacy-format images, and all 36 without intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate right-sized AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, preserve dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold imagery.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the landing-page resource budget before user intent.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins account for 2.30 MB of 2.46 MB transferred and 143 of 158 requests, including player, analytics and fingerprinting resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer player and measurement code until interaction/consent, and remove low-value vendors.

findings.summary: Repeated feed scrolling produced large retained-heap growth.
findings.evidence: After ten bottom/top scroll cycles, the heap summary grew from 53,877,211 to 74,824,271 self-size bytes (+39%), nodes from 1,144,725 to 1,622,430 (+42%), and closures from 104,937 to 160,682. Separate fresh sessions introduce variance, so leak attribution is medium-confidence, but the growth warrants same-session profiling.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat the baseline/interaction/final snapshots in one session, trace retainers for growing objects/closures, and clean up card observers, listeners, media/player state and caches when content leaves the viewport.

findings.summary: The initial discovery page has a large memory footprint for a browsing grid.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 1,144,725 nodes, 5,112,107 edges, 53.9 MB self size and 104,937 closures before sustained use.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or bound offscreen feed state, delay player construction, reduce retained closures, and define a memory budget for the discovery route.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI include insufficient-contrast color pairs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found seven color-contrast failures across the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct each reported foreground/background pair to meet WCAG contrast minimums in default and preference-driven themes.

findings.summary: A set of visible controls is too small for dependable touch and reflow use.
findings.evidence: The interaction probe counted 18 visible focusable targets under 24 CSS px in at least one dimension, although the 360 px layout itself did not overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase control hit areas to at least the WCAG minimum and test 200% zoom plus narrow reflow without obscured controls.

findings.summary: The account authentication path relies on password entry without a phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The login path exposes username/email and password fields but no page use of navigator.credentials or PublicKeyCredential; account creation is also CAPTCHA-gated.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys alongside the password fallback, keep recovery explicit, and document clear account cancellation and reauthentication paths.

taskList.title: Server-render public content and resilient 404/recovery states
Cut startup JavaScript, long tasks and third-party transfer
Fix accessible names, focus, heading order, contrast and target sizing
Harden CSP, browser policies and cookie flags
Make consent balanced and defer nonessential tracking
Reserve and right-size responsive image geometry
Profile and bound retained memory in one long-lived session
Add passkeys, labels and autofill tokens to account forms
Respect color-scheme, reduced-motion and contrast preferences
